items.stem:
Because the observatory stored thousands of photographic plates Cannon could study the same stars repeatedly. Her classifications helped astronomers identify distant stars, compare their temperatures, and trace changes in stellar populations. By 1922, Cannon's system had become standard practice at observatories in several countries. The system was easy to learn, so assistants could apply it to thousands of plates. Cannon continued classifying stars for decades, and her catalog eventually supported later research on the structure of the Milky Way.
